title: Charcoal Briquettes 8kg

drivers.name: Halloween (week before)
drivers.evidence: Classical model uses two past occurrences, but noise-adjusted effect is x0.68 (median). Past weeks show high variability (x0.29, x0.74), and effect is not consistently replicable. Product noise is 73%, so x0.68 is near noise floor. No evidence of stronger effect this year.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 28.6. No events or price changes are scheduled for the target week. The classical uplift model suggests a 32% drop due to Halloween, but this is based on only two past occurrences and the noise-adjusted effect is x0.68. However, the product shows no consistent Halloween effect: past Halloween weeks had mixed results (x0.29, x0.74), and the noise-adjusted estimate is only x0.68—close to 1.0. Given the product’s high ordinary-week noise (73%) and lack of a strong, repeatable pattern, the Halloween effect is not reliably predictive. No promotion or price change is planned. The baseline trend shows a 32.2% decline over 13 weeks, but this is already reflected in the baseline. No other drivers justify adjustment.

It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-73% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
